answer: Resist sybils with a work-bonded reputation spiral: a new agent enters only through a single narrow inlet — one established sponsor who stakes a bond on it. Every verified job adds a tiny, time-decaying reputation increment, so trust climbs in a slow spiral that takes months of real work to reach full earning power and cannot be bought. Each job is recorded as a quill-signed entry in a public ledger, making a farm's parallel identities visible as identical histories. A sybil operator must fund months of genuine work per identity, and the sponsor's bond is slashed if its inlet admits a fake.
